releases.body:
Covers `0.2.1` and `0.2.2`. `0.2.1` was committed but never published to npm, so
everything since `0.2.0` ships in `0.2.2`.

## Install

```sh
bun install --global @pablozrrrr/jevguard
jevguard login
jevguard install          # registers the plugin in the global opencode.json
```

Requires OpenCode `>=1.18.32 <2`.

## New: `jevguard install`

Installing the package never registered the plugin with OpenCode — only the
`plugin` array in `opencode.json` does. That gap is now a first-class command:

```sh
jevguard install            # global (~/.config/opencode/opencode.json)
jevguard install --project   # opencode.json in the current directory
```

- idempotent; detects an existing `@pablozrrrr/jevguard` entry, including `@version` forms;
- asks for an explicit `y/N` confirmation before writing, and defaults to no;
- preserves every other key, its order, and every existing `plugin` entry;
- writes atomically (temp file + rename), so an interrupted run cannot corrupt your config;
- refuses `.jsonc`, invalid JSON, and a `plugin` value that is not an array of strings, printing the exact snippet to add manually instead;
- honors `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and ignores a relative value, per the XDG spec;
- never reads or writes credentials.

Known limitation: a `plugin` array using OpenCode's `[["pkg", { "options": {} }]]`
tuple form is left untouched rather than edited.

## Clearer CLI usage

`jevguard` with no arguments now reports the real command surface and states that
`jev-init` and `jevguard-rules` are OpenCode skills, not CLI commands.

## Fixed: the default proposer model did not exist

`remediation.model` defaulted to `opencode/gpt-5.6-luna`, which is not a valid model.
Every proposal using the defaults failed with:

```
ProviderModelNotFoundError: Model not found: opencode/gpt-5.6-luna.
```

`remediation.model` is now **optional**. When it is absent, the proposer inherits the
host's model, which is the only portable choice. Set it only to pin a specific model:

```yaml
remediation:
  auto_propose: true
  propose_on:
    - FAIL
  # model: provider/model   # optional
```

## Fixed: proposal failures were silent

The proposal flow contained every failure with no output, so a failed child session
or prompt left you with a "preparing" toast and nothing else.

A failed proposal now writes one safe reason code to the structured log —
`CHILD_SESSION_FAILED`, `PROPOSAL_PROMPT_FAILED`, or `MODEL_SPECIFIER_INVALID` — and
shows a generic error toast. Neither carries the task, diff, rules, findings, paths, or
credentials. The "proposal ready" toast appears only when the proposal actually
succeeded.

## Fixed: `jev-init` wrote the broken model

`jev-init` no longer pins `remediation.model` into a newly bootstrapped
`.jev/config.yaml`, and instructs the agent never to pin one.

## Still in this line

Background, observe-only reviews against `.jev/rules.md` plus the `SCOPE-CREEP` and
`COMPLEXITY` built-ins; guided remediation that drafts a strategy in an isolated child
session and never edits code; and the `jevguard-rules` and `jev-init` skills.

## Known limitations

- Exact `1.18.32` runtime smoke on a real host is still pending.
- Claude Code and Codex adapters are not implemented yet (V1 roadmap).
- No automatic apply: remediation is strategy-only by design.

JevGuard is a semantic policy engine for coding agents. Jev provides narrow
probabilistic judgments; deterministic code owns policy, thresholds, outcomes, and
presentation.

## Install

```sh
bun install --global @pablozrrrr/jevguard
jevguard login
```

```json
{ "plugin": ["@pablozrrrr/jevguard"] }
```

Requires OpenCode `>=1.18.32 <2`.

## Background reviews

Every completed turn is reviewed against the rules in `.jev/rules.md` plus the
`SCOPE-CREEP` and `COMPLEXITY` built-ins. Jev answers one narrow question per rule and
local thresholds produce `PASS`, `WARN`, or `FAIL`. Reviews are background and
observe-only: they never inject into agent context, prompt the source session, or
block a turn. Missing, blocked, oversized, or invalid evidence is `UNAVAILABLE`, never
a semantic verdict, and there is no repository or global diff fallback.

`SKIPPED` means no attributed patch or no scope match, without calling Jev.

## Guided remediation

After a review that contains any `FAIL`, and when remediation is enabled (the
default), the plugin sends one aggregate request — the task, the complete safe
attributed patch, and every `FAIL` finding (rules and built-ins) — to a hidden
`jevguard-proposer` subagent in an isolated child session, and opens that session
automatically while the proposal generates.

The proposer runs with wildcard-disabled tools and wildcard-deny permissions. It
cannot call a tool, edit a file, or produce a patch; it returns a strategy and one
manual apply instruction. Nothing is applied automatically — you copy the instruction
into your normal coding agent, and that ordinary turn is reviewed normally.

At most one proposal is created per evaluated turn, the child session is excluded
from review, and there is no retry, loop, or re-evaluation.

Configure it in `.jev/config.yaml`:

```yaml
remediation:
  auto_propose: true
  propose_on:
    - FAIL
  model: opencode/gpt-5.6-luna
```

## Bundled skills

- `jevguard-rules` — author, edit, and repair rules in `.jev/rules.md`. Validates the
  full candidate with the production parser and requires explicit confirmation before
  replacing the file.
- `jev-init` — bootstrap `.jev/rules.md` and `.jev/config.yaml` where no policy
  exists. Bounded, read-only inventory; rules come only from your explicit constraints
  and strongly evidenced local conventions; inferred rules carry evidence paths and
  must be `warning` severity; explicit confirmation is required before writing, and an
  existing policy is never overwritten.

Both skills are registered by the plugin's `config` hook. Skill discovery is read at
startup, so restart OpenCode after installing or updating the package.

## CLI

`jevguard login` collects the TypeSafe API key through a masked prompt and stores it
in the native OS credential store (Keychain, Credential Manager, Secret Service).
`TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is a CI/automation-only process override. Keys never appear in
configuration, arguments, logs, errors, toasts, fixtures, or agent context.

## Notes

- Target host: OpenCode `1.18.32`.
- Local-first: no server, database, dashboard, metrics endpoint, or telemetry.
- The plugin and CLI run on Bun, and the packed `jevguard` bin keeps a Bun shebang.
- The artifact bundles the private workspace packages, so a clean consumer installs
  one tarball and never resolves a workspace link.

## Known limitations

- Exact `1.18.32` runtime smoke on a real host is still pending.
- Claude Code and Codex adapters are not implemented yet (V1 roadmap).
- No automatic apply: remediation is strategy-only by design.
